title: Electron Ledger: The Static Workshop
summary: Run a static-charge workshop: pump and rub bodies to fill customer orders, then work out which materials give electrons away.
subject: physics
concepts: Charge from electron count, q = N e
learningOutcome: The student can predict the sign each body gets when two are rubbed, find the electrons needed for a given charge, and order materials by how easily they lose electrons.

levels.title: Pump it
levels.adds: Baseline: only electrons move. Work out the charge needed to attract or repel a body, then pump electrons on or off.
hints: First decide what charge the other body has: gaining electrons makes a body negative, losing them makes it positive.
Like charges repel and unlike charges attract, so that tells you the charge your sphere needs.
A negative body has gained electrons and a positive one has lost them. Protons never move.

levels.title: Rub two bodies
levels.adds: New idea: rubbing moves electrons from one body to the other, so both are charged, with opposite signs.
hints: Rub different pairs and watch what each one becomes.
Whatever one body loses, the other gains.
A material can be positive with one partner and negative with another.

levels.title: Count the electrons
levels.adds: New idea: charge comes from a count of electrons, q = N e. Convert the order to a stroke count.
hints: N = q / e, and the strokes are N divided by the electrons per stroke.
Both bodies end with the same size of charge, with opposite signs.

levels.title: Who gives way?
levels.adds: New idea: materials have an order. Test pairs, then chain the results to rank all four pads.
hints: Each rub tells you which pad gives electrons to which.
If A gives to B and B gives to C, then A gives to C. No rub needed.
The pad that never gains electrons from the others goes first.

misconceptions: Protons are what move between rubbed solids
A body that loses electrons stays neutral
